summary: The exact candidate fixes and correctly values the issue's fully-past-prompt EAGLE3 draft-extend case, but remains cardinality-incorrect when an extend starts inside precomputed multimodal positions and crosses their end. Because that independent boundary case still provides fewer mRoPE columns than forwarded tokens, this is a partial source fix rather than a complete enforcement of the original contract.

tests.what_was_measured: The untouched base produced [3,10] positions for 40 tokens in the original scenario and [3,2] positions for a four-token crossing extend.
All four candidate CPU tests passed against the exact checked-out candidate source.
The candidate fixed the original fully-past-prompt shape to [3,40], but the independent cross-boundary case remained [3,2] instead of [3,4].
On gfx950, the ordinary ragged candidate output exactly matched an independent reference, then the cross-boundary assertion failed because four tokens received only two positions.

gpu_execution.evidence: reports/j-ae2eedac3bc7/raw/gpu-inventory.log identifies one AMD Instinct MI355X with capability (9,5); candidate-gpu-contract.log records exact reference equality and the failing boundary assertion on cuda:0 (PyTorch's ROCm device API).

remaining_counterexamples.case: A multimodal extend begins two tokens before the end of a 16-column precomputed mRoPE tensor and extends four tokens.
remaining_counterexamples.expected: mrope_positions shape [3,4], one column per forwarded token
remaining_counterexamples.actual: mrope_positions shape [3,2] on both CPU and gfx950 because the non-empty partial slice bypasses the fallback

remaining_limitations: No Qwen3-VL or EAGLE3 weights were available. The full serving path, CUDA/H100 fused Triton kernel, semantic output comparison, performance, multi-GPU, and multi-node behavior remain unverified. The available architecture was one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) under ROCm 7.2. The change is Python-only, so no native rebuild was applicable.
